body.x: Medical device developer ‘MVITRO’ announced its participation in CES 2025, the world’s largest electronics and IT expo, held from January 7 to 10, 2025, in Las Vegas, USA.

MVITRO, a specialist in home care medical devices, has completed the development of a product integrating a nearly pain-free laser blood collection device and glucose meter and is preparing for its launch. At CES 2025, they will introduce the FOOTIV model, a home care device aimed at preventing diabetic foot diseases, as they seek an innovation award and make strides toward global expansion.

FOOTIV integrates PPG sensors and Biothesiometry technology to allow anyone at home to easily and precisely measure foot sensory status, blood flow speed, and oxygen saturation. It also provides a comprehensive foot health monitoring solution by generating quantified risk assessment scores for developing diabetic foot ulcers based on AI.

Currently, up to 35% of diabetic patients are at risk of developing diabetic foot ulcers, among whom 20% may lead to amputation, and 10% could result in death. One significant risk of diabetic complications is that patients may not realize how serious their condition is until it progresses significantly.
MVITRO expects that “FOOTIV will greatly assist diabetic patients in managing their foot health effectively at home, thereby preventing diseases and reducing the risk of complications.”

At CES 2023 and 2024, MVITRO gained significant attention from global attendees and buyers by introducing ORTIV, the world’s first painless laser blood collection device with a glucose meter. ORTIV is awaiting approval from the FDA and KFDA, with authorization expected within 2024.
